elements.element: Customer has no obligation to give Vendor terms as favourable as, or more favourable than, terms Customer gives any third party.
elements.evidence: Section 7.2 expressly states that Customer is not required to offer such terms, and Section 12.3 confirms that Customer has made no most-favoured-customer commitment.

elements.element: If Customer is subject to an MFN obligation, that obligation is limited to a specifically defined product.
elements.evidence: The condition is demonstrably absent: the rendered language imposes no MFN obligation on Customer, so no product limitation is needed.

elements.element: If Customer is subject to an MFN obligation, that obligation lasts no more than 12 months.
elements.evidence: The condition is demonstrably absent: Sections 7.2 and 12.3 establish that Customer has no MFN obligation, so there is no duration requiring limitation.

elements.element: If Customer is subject to an MFN obligation, comparisons are limited to reasonably comparable transactions, with carve-outs for material differences.
elements.evidence: The condition is demonstrably absent: no MFN comparison obligation remains. These comparison protections would be necessary only if an MFN were imposed.

result.reason: The narrow change to Section 7.2 converts the affirmative MFN duty into an express statement that Customer has no such duty. It aligns with the unchanged acknowledgment in Section 12.3, adds no unrelated requirement, and leaves unrelated commercial terms intact. The fallback elements are satisfied because their triggering condition—an MFN burdening Customer—is demonstrably absent, not because the clause contains express product, duration, or comparability limits.
